findings.title: [P2] Upload the assembler proof with the compact candidate
findings.trigger: Use the compact-universal-UNSIGNED-experiment artifact from a successful compact-engine workflow run for downstream signing and release inventory generation.
findings.body: The assembler invoked at line 65 writes compact-universal-unsigned.runtime-proof.json beside its APK, but this upload includes only the aligned APK and checksum. No other step uploads the proof, so it disappears with the package runner. tools/generate_sbom.py now requires --engine-proof and checks that proof's per-ABI engine/configuration records and payload hash against the final APK. A consumer of the workflow's candidate cannot complete that checked SBOM path using the supplied artifacts, even though native engines are available separately. Include the original runtime-proof JSON in this candidate artifact; its payload binding intentionally survives the subsequent alignment/signing steps.
evidence: assemble_compact_experiment.py:89 names its sibling .runtime-proof.json and :246 writes it
compact-engine.yml:72-74 uploads only aligned APK and SHA256SUMS
generate_sbom.py:73 requires --engine-proof; :81-100 loads proof and verifies final payload
findings.scope_limit: This is a broken evidence handoff for workflow-produced candidates, not a claim that an unverified APK was already published.

findings.title: [P3] Update the compact build recipe to the current required arguments
findings.trigger: Follow the documented compact universal Build shell commands against the current tools.
findings.body: The assembler command supplies no --ffmpeg-version or --lame-version, while the current script explicitly calls argparse.error unless both numeric versions are supplied for replacement-engine mode; therefore the documented recipe stops before producing its unsigned candidate. The final audit command also omits the mandatory report positional argument required by audit_elf_alignment.py. Refresh the recipe to use the pinned versions/current runtime overrides and include an output report path so the documented release preparation path actually runs.

verified_observations: android.yml runs on main/maintenance/feature pushes, v* tags, pull requests and manual dispatch. Its permissions are contents:read, and it does not create/update GitHub releases or upload APKs as official downloads.

compact-engine.yml publishes CI artifacts explicitly named UNSIGNED experiment. Its automatic trigger is restricted to the named feature branch and native recipe/workflow paths; manual dispatch remains available. It does not sign or publish official releases.

Production Gradle signing uses owner-provided environment values; absent those inputs, release builds remain unsigned. CI emulator packages use a temporary generated test key, and the workflows do not reference production signing secrets.

The API29-36 device matrix uses shared Python packaging with upstream FFmpeg and a terminal JUnit OK-result assertion, rather than treating adb instrument's process exit alone as test success. Existing historical documentation explicitly separates that matrix from signed compact-release acceptance and discloses skipped opt-in network cases.

The checkpoint marks current launch work unpublished, records pending/full-lint and emulator acceptance work, and retains the older RC5 verification as historical artifact evidence. No claim of completed current launch certification was inferred from the older files.
The compact package job performs testDebugUnitTest, lintRelease and assembleRelease before size/checksum/upload; it is not represented here as signed-release runtime acceptance.

Gradle wrapper distribution has a pinned SHA-256. Native recipe pins FFmpeg commit, LAME source digest and NDK version; runtime override fetch/assembly verifies pinned archive and library hashes and ABI identities.
limitations: No live remote workflow state, branch protection settings, release downloads or signing certificates were fetched or independently reverified.
No requirement for automatic official publication, all-ABI device tests, automatic lintRelease on every source push or a new security certification gate was invented.
Source/workflow review cannot establish that a particular final APK passed acceptance; that remains separate artifact/device evidence owned by the parent workflow.
